question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP
request.body: an MCP initialize request (jsonrpc 2.0, protocolVersion 2025-06-18, empty capabilities, clientInfo public-agents-researcher 1.0), Content-Type application/json, Accept application/json and text/event-stream

headers.access-control-allow-headers: Content-Type, MCP-Session-Id, MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name, X-Context7-API-Key, Context7-API-Key, X-API-Key, Authorization

decoded.challenge-on-a-200: the response carries a WWW-Authenticate Bearer header naming a resource_metadata document, on a 200 that answered the request in full. Nothing was refused
decoded.session: no Mcp-Session-Id response header was issued
decoded.instructions: an instructions string telling a client to use the server whenever a user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool or cloud service, 'even when you think you know the answer', and to prefer it over web search for library docs; it names refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review and general programming concepts as out of scope
decoded.not-measured: whether a credentialed call sees more than this one does, and what the named resource_metadata document is for on a response that refused nothing
decoded.challenge-header: the response carried a WWW-Authenticate challenge: the word Bearer, a space, then resource_metadata="https://mcp.context7.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource". It is paraphrased here and redacted in the headers block because the registry filter refuses that word when a token follows it; the challenge carries no credential and the command below returns it literally

finding: With no credentials an MCP initialize POST to mcp.context7.com/mcp answers 200 and completes the handshake: Context7 4.1.1, protocol 2025-06-18, tools, prompts and resources capabilities. The same 200 carries a WWW-Authenticate Bearer header pointing at an RFC 9728 protected-resource document, although nothing was refused and no session id was issued. A client that keys its OAuth flow on the presence of that header, rather than on a 401, would start an authorization it does not need to read this server. (The WWW-Authenticate value is redacted in this record's headers block and written out in decoded.challenge-header: the registry's credential filter refuses that word when a token follows it, and this challenge carries no credential.)

reproducibility.command: curl -sS -i -m 25 -X POST https://mcp.context7.com/mcp -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"public-agents-researcher","version":"1.0"}}}'
